E001.text:
The boat was purchased from Joe Martinez III of San Antonio on December 1st 1994. Lester
Ducote went with me to San Antonio to close the sale and haul the boat, "Knock Down" to Austin. Bill Peace went with me to haul the boat to Port Aransas.

December 15th arrangements were made with Dumas Marine for compounding, waxing, bottom paint, teak work, etc. Island Boat Works handled the electronic tune up and the installation of trim tabs, Lowrance 350 GPS, washdown, etc. Many short runs up Lydia Ann Waterway or toward Corpus Christi were made during this shakedown period.
E001.note: From conversations with Captain Eddie it sounds like there were a few shakedown runs also made on Lake Austin. Got to find out more about that, it's wild to picture the Seahawk running up the lake towards Pennybacker at 35 knots.

E004.text: Bill Hudspeth and Val England join Mike and me for a great snapper trip! 80 degrees off the bar to Big Red in 21 fathoms. We used cut squid (big ones!) to catch 2 large sow snapper - 24lbs and 20lbs and another 20 or so smaller ones. Beautiful weather, no seas, light north wind. Cruising speed out and back was 25 knots.
E004.note: Big Red an oil platform painted in red primer paint. I'm curious what the navigational reference of 80 degrees off the bar means.

E-9b5808e48b.text:
Bill Hudspeth, Mike Fleming & I fish a rig located at N27°53.152, W96°44.925. Mike caught a big king - weight unknown, but he  was 55 inches long and had a 24 inch girth. 2 other 15 pound kings, then Mike caught an atlantic sharpnose that made his trip!

Wind ENE 15 knots. Rough but lots of sunshine. Good time!

E-8dd394a776.text: Memorial Day Weekend - Wind still Howling - got out Saturday with Frank Niendorf, sons David and Will and of course Mike Fleming. Went back to above noted rig - caught one shark - missed two others. Seas got to 6-8' so we came in.
E-8dd394a776.note: I was pissed off because Frank missed a gaff on my white tip shark. The next day there was a handwritten note on the steering wheel in a child's writing that read "no one allowed on this boat that doesn't know how to gaff"

E-77f97f0ab3.text: Too rough for us to take Seahawk out so Mike and I go out on the Wharf Cat. Rough seas. Mike wins pot of $51 with a 12lb King! Maybe sometime this summer the wind will stop!
E-77f97f0ab3.note: The Wharf Cat is a big 72 foot catamaran that operates out of Fisherman's Wharf in Port A. it would make daily runs out to the rigs a short ways off the coast and everyone on board would drop weighted lines on the down current side for snapper. Being larger it was better suited to big seas. Wind hardly ever stopped that summer, says the captain.

E-f80d412081.text: Bill Hudspeth, Mike & I fish Scorpion Rig - we catch two king and three shark, in one hour.
E-f80d412081.note: Scoprion Rig had two big cranes coming off the sides, looked like one was its tail and one was its head.

E-aabe25e19a.text: 1st day of the Deep Sea Roundup Tournament - Gary Einkhoff, Me, Lester, Alex & Michael head out in 6 foot seas to just short of Big Red. Squalls convince us to head N-NW to Mighty Whitey Rig. Windy. We catch a 33 pounder (Lester), a 22 pounder (Alex) and a 22 pounder (Mike). Alex & Mike were in first and second place at end of day one.
E-aabe25e19a.note: Dad says this was a rough day, six foot seas! Mighty Whitey Rig was an inshore rig painted entirely white.

E-6275f088f2.text: We head out on 78° to Big Red - beautiful day! Running 3,000 RPM all day. Not much luck at Big Red or Val's Rig. Then we go to Satellite Rig. Alex catches a 22 pound snapper that wins the junior and senior division of the tournament for snapper. We also catch 20 or so other snapper 2 pounds to 6 pounds. We trolled back in with no takers except amberjack. We caught and released several short of legal limit.

E-15669bb080.text: Outboard tournament - Mike, Einkauf & me. Beautiful seas - all the way to Baker Reef. No luck! 10 gallons per hour.
E-15669bb080.note: They split up the tournament by engine spec, so the outboard tournament was our time to shine. Baker Reef was one of the coral reefs offshore. Baker, South Baker, Southern, and Hospital were all about 40 miles out. They catch marlin, sailfish, and wahoo out there.

E-243dafc8f0.text: Went North to the Way Ups then East to Satellite. 10 snappers, lots of chicken dolphin in weed lines. Other than that no luck trolling - beautiful calm day  10 gallons per hour.
E-243dafc8f0.note: The Way Ups were a cluster of rigs about 35 miles North of the jetty's that were in shallow water. A dolphin is another name for a mahi mahi. Chicken dolphin is just a little mahi mahi, usually 3-10 pounds.

E-06e80bdd06.text: Took Mike hornsby and friend, Jenny, to Lone Pipe. Caught 6 Kings in about 20 minutes - came home in beautiful weather. Depth recorder out, also fuel pump between the auxilary and the main fuel line must have a constriction. Next week don't buy bait - we have 20 pounds of squid and ribbon fish in the freezer.
E-06e80bdd06.note: Lone Pipe was just a big ol' standpipe gas well sticking out of the water. Covered in barnacles, which attract fish.

E-d779898898.text: Guests were Dr Scott Holt and Dr Steve ___ from the University of Texas Marine Science Center. We left at 6:30 am. Calm seas. Went to Scorpion, only one king, then to Val's Rig where the current was running so swiftly to the North that we could not tie on.
E-d779898898.note: They ended up naming Val's Rig after Val England where she caught those snapper there in one of the earlier trips.

E-be19a07009.text:
July 29, 1995, continued

We proceeded off shore about 1/2 mile where we found a great sargassom weed line. 
We stopped and chummed up six dolphin (3 to 4 lbs) and a 15 lb Wahoo. Dr. Holt's first Wahoo and Dr Steve's first Dolphin. We Ended the day at Big Red, catching and 27 Vermillion and red Snapper - Seas roughed up way home - N. wind 3-4 ft - Tropical Depression heading our way. Wahoo and Dolphin caught on Ballyhoo under an Octopus skirt
E-be19a07009.note:
This is a continuation of the last entry on the previous page, I need to combine them. 

Vermillion are a type of snapper bright red as the name implies even brighter than red snapper, with some yellow along the gill plates. More importantly there wasn't a limit on them at the time, according to the Captain.

E-61f45f40e7.text: Charles and Judy Durban; after 2 days of waiting out Tropical Storm Gabriela, we make it out on a heading 85° to 95 feet of water - lots of shrimp boats. Caught 6 kings real fast, no size though - all 12-20 lbs. Squally day - 4' to 5' seas, some rain. Again we used ballyhoo under seven string octopus yellow and green. One great bait!
E-61f45f40e7.note: This entry should actually be dated August 13. Mentioned a few times before, ballyhoo are a great bait for mahi mahi and other fish. Small, about 10 inches long and with a big beak coming out from their lower jaw.

E-8f1abd29f1.text:
Chris Carothers, Mike Fleming, Nicole Beasley & me. Beautiful day! We leave at 7:00 - hit weed line at 80 degrees in about 19 fathoms. Caught two nice dolphin. 10 -12 pounds. Weed line was patchy, and only about 300 yds, long. Seas running from the southeast to the north west. Then we go to Val's Rig past Big Red where we caught a limit of kings (12). A big shark (unseen but big by bite angle) cut three of our kings off right behind the gills! Fast action on kings, 2 on at at once a few times! Also caught 8 or so snapper, one at 6 lbs the largest.

I was the only witness. The shark was about as big as a suburban. It had at least 25 stripes. It probably was 325 pounds.
E-8f1abd29f1.note: That bottom note is from me, Mike. I remember seeing that big sucker come up under the boat as we were tied off on the rig! Everyone must have been sick of me because no one wanted to come up and look at it. Too bad, they missed out!

E-5a8d69156d.text: Dr. Scott Holt & Dr. Joan Holt on board with Mike and me. We ended up going north to the Way Ups. No kings taken. Not much sign of life until we tied on to a Way Up and caught a limit of nice snapper, released a 10 pound king. Beautiful day.

E-2e540d032d.text: Cameron Pratt, Lester Ducote, Mike Fleming, Alex Ducote, Will Cardwell and me head out to Big Blue. Pretty day but choppy with North wind. Not a strike at Blue! Starboard engine flooded out. Proceed to Port Aransas. Trolling along the way caught a Spanish mackerel. And then we tied on one rig, opposite of Perry Bass's house! Will at that rig caught 3 small ling, and Alex caught one huge one!! Headed in. Engine started when lifted to clean carburetor! Bad day
E-2e540d032d.note: Mike was probably pissed he didn't get a ling cause he loved them so much. Perry Basset was a big millionaire and chairman of the UT mine science board. Did a ton of good environmentally down there, whatever Parks and Wildlife wanted he'd tried to fund. Engine trouble offshore always makes your stomach churn a little bit, says the Captain.

E-88c0444433.text: Lester Ducote and I start the morning at Baker. Anchored up on the main rock of North Baker. Limited on Kings in 10 minutes.Then trolled marlin lures to Dunnbar. No strikes. About noon we went to the main oil platform in inside of Dunnbar- A7 in 33 fathoms. Limited on nice snapper. Three break offs on some really big (!!) bottom fish. Probably amberjack. Also saw some huge barracuda - 50 pounds plus. Caught a small 10 pounder that won his division of this weekend’s Corpus Christi Big Game Club tournament. At 2 o’clock we headed in looking for weed lines. Found one only about 50 yard 500 yards long in 30 fathoms. We trolled ballyhoo under seven strand octopus, skirts, yellow and green and red and black. Three really nice bull dolphin 20 to 35 pounds and three smaller chicken. Agreat calm day all the way home at 30 to 32 mph. Used 10 gallons per minute.

E-83492c806c.text:
This entry should actually be dated September 16. 

Mike me and Gary Schmitt and wife Kathleen on board. North to Way Ups then to Satellite and then A7. Rough day, no fish (12 snapper!) To hell with going out when it’s so rough. 198 Fish so far this season (Sunday). 115 gallons - filled up and topped off with the oil - ready for next time. GPS started acting up as if power was shorting out. Long and lat would stay on, course over the ground and speed in miles per hour.The lower display consisting of true bearing and estimated time of arrival and distance to go would vanish, then the whole screen would go. I would push way point Port Aransas Jetty (this happened 55 miles out on the way in) then the whole screen would come back after about five minutes to re-require satellites. Very strange. We are checking the wiring today and if they’re ok we will send the unit back to Tulsa for fixing. Yesterday was really rough and it’s possible that something might have jarred loose.

Yesterday at A7 I baited the line with a live snapper on a single number eight hook - 120 pound wire on a 50 lb Penn and tossed it out to drift as we snapper fished. A big barracuda nailed him and I pushed the drag all the way up to stop him from getting under the rig. Stopped him and he made several short high speed runs slashing back and forth and the damned hook pulled out. I think a new state record ‘cuda lives there and I’m going to try him at every opportunity.
E-83492c806c.note: From the Captain: I remember that bastard. I dealt with him many days after that. God he was just there and he would lay out working his gills and look up at me.

E-34da3b6c76.text: First trip out since 9/16. Went to Big Red, Val, and A7 with Scott Holt - great day of weather but short of fish. 9 snapper.

E-cd1dda3a99.text: Rick Vaughn, Fred Dipple & me go to Big Red, and North.- 1 king, 2 jacks, and 3 snapper.

E-9de191931a.text: Rough, 5-6 ft. Went South for 5 miles, we caught 2 jacks, Rick Vaughn fought & landed one in 45 min that was 25 lbs class.
E-9de191931a.note: Can't believe I went out in this shit, he says.

E-a6ebca7c9a.text:
Mike Gillespie, Mike Fleming and I leave the jetty at 9:00. At 90° MF decides it’s too rough (smart boy!) so we take him back to the dock. Mike G and I then go to the three standpipes 120° off bar. We catch 2 kings, one Atlantic sharp nose shark - and a large jack crevalle, about 30 lbs.

Swells 3-5' out of southwest. A norther arrives earlier than expected and a marine warning went out [over the radio] to return to port because of 60 knot winds, in a squall line just then hitting Rockport. We covered those 6 miles at 32 knot speed and hit the jetty just as it hit. Cold wind - saw a waterspout forming in the channel. Glad to be home.

E-51a6d90868.text:
Beautiful day with a cool north wind not 10-15 knots. Seas 3-5 ft from NE/ESW. Went to same stand pipes as before, Mike is entered in the GCCA tournament, so we're looking for the big ones. No luck trolling today, so I rig a sea anchor off the bow that swings the Seahawk broadside to the swells, and I set up a chum line - this works!! We catch 3 kings and one shark in about 30 minutes with 3 other hard strikes breaking off. Crew is getting queasy so we returns to port to drop Gillespie off. Mike F and I run up the channel to Pelican Island where we anchor looking for reds & trout. Mike catches one big 2 pound hard head.

The weigh in at at Woody's was fun! I string Mike's catch of the two kings, one shark, and a hardhead on a loop of line and he drags it to the weight in booth. Every kid wins something, Mike won for biggest kingfish so he received a trophy and a really nice kingfish rod. We head to Bilmore's and purchase a 209 Penn Reel to celebrate his feat and complete his rig. A real fun day.

E-8baeaf29ad.text: Beautiful day. Mike (Fleming), me, Patrick (Fleming), and friend Josh went to Stand Pipes south of P.A. in 40 feet of water. We caught 1 king, one 39' ling trolling, then caught two more kings (drifting + chumming). Patrick and Josh were getting a little mal de mer, so we left for home. Mike caught his first King on his new kingfish rig - it really is smooth.
E-8baeaf29ad.note: Real close off port a, real go to spot if the kings were in. Mal de mer is sickness of the sea, according to the captain

E-b06f4bea44.text: Mike G, Meredith and David (honeymooners) and me try to catch some kingfish. Pretty day, 10-15mph S.E. winds. Went to same standpipe as on 6/13, no luck, then west to Big Platform - we caught two kings (drifting and one trolling), lost 4 others that made long runs then broke free - very disappointing day.

E-dcead6d0b5.text: Dick Chote, Art Shepherd and Bryan (Dick's son in law) on board - Limit of kings, in close - run to Mighty Whitey for snapper - no keepers. Rough as hell!

E-1047d68004.text: Same crew - hooked a tarpon at the jetty! Fought him 3 hours and 45 min! Dick Chote did a fine job - broke the line as we were about to gaff him for pictures. Great Day!

E-f8a3942aec.text: July 5 - Bill Hudspeth, Morgan Stone & me go to Southern — beautiful day + almost flat however fishing was slow. Caught one bonito at Southern on the way to the Jack Up Rig. Finally came in to the South Standpipes and caught 4 king’s.
E-f8a3942aec.note: Jack Up Rig was in a little oil field south of PA. It has all been wiped out by hurricanes since then. You could tell they were reworking Jack Up at the time because it had big cranes all over it.

E002.text: The first offshore trip was made in rough weather, 4-5 knot wind. NNE out to 16 fathoms looking for snapper. Cameron Pratt and Bill Hudspeth were with me. A dark rough day not conducive to fun fishing - we caught 2 snapper (too small) and a few triggers and called it a day.
E002.note: A lot of these trips will use a direction and a depth as shorthand for navigation purposes. Captain Ed would maintain a heading on the compass from the jetty, where most of our trips began, follow it out to a certain depth. The sea floor out in the Gulf is a gradual slope so doing this would result in arriving at nearly the same spot with only the use of a compass and a depth finder.

E003.text: Patricia & Mike go with me on an impromptu snapper trip, beautiful weather - no fish.

E-4eb0fe8c4f.text: Lester and I try to fish outside jetty for spanish mackerel - Rough seas! 5' and close together. 2 on, lost both.

E-e4f7ea18f5.text: First day of Deep Sea Roundup - Mike, Alex, Lester & me head first to Satellite and then to Apache. At Apache we trolled by and picked up a medium barracuda that won the Junior Division for Alex. Mike caught another barracuda 5-6 lbs and two rainbow runners. Real slow -- first time to use the squid family! It looked good but received no strikes.
